findings.summary: The four new integration cases genuinely compose the real G6/G8 seams and are deterministic.
findings.detail: GoalG6G8IntegrationTests.cs composes real product seams rather than restating constants: operator display values are converted through the code-owned ByteLimitUnits/ByteLimitField mapping, serialized as a JSON-number Limits object, deserialized with the pinned JsonDefaults.Options (the same option set the GoalAIntegrationTests precedent uses for the elevation-gated PluginsController POST), passed through the real Plugin.UpdateConfiguration override (validate -> base persist -> activate), and read back from a real XML file boundary via TestXmlSerializer (a genuine System.Xml.Serialization wrapper). The two byte-path cases assert the exact bytes on the deserialized candidate, ConfigurationSnapshotService.Current, and the persisted file, and assert the store -> display -> store identity. The min/default/max case covers all seven fields and all three 64 KiB minima (ProviderResponseLimitBytes, SourceArtifactLimitBytes, DerivedArtifactLimitBytes display as 0.0625 MB). The two G8 cases compose the code-owned RestartRequiredSettings classification against the embedded page's restartRequiredFields mirror (exact equality), the static note markup (exact set and per-setting string, mixed clause iff mixed), the submit-handler detection domain, and the modal message. The intersection case pins the four restart-required byte limits across the mapping table, native input step, note, and reminder domain. Tests are deterministic (GUID temp root, disposed; no timing or concurrency), pass 4/4 focused and in both full-suite runs.
evidence: dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~GoalG6G8IntegrationTests -> Failed 0, Passed 4, Skipped 0, Total 4

findings.summary: The page's inline JavaScript conversion and modal are verified structurally only; server-side step rejection is not exercised end-to-end.
findings.detail: The page's byte conversion (config.html byteLimitToByte/byteLimitToDisplay) and the Dashboard.alert modal cannot be executed in this repository or environment (no JS runtime present; the pinned live host runs --nowebclient), so the integration cases pin them as exact strings over the embedded page resource and the conversion is exercised as real C# through ByteLimitUnits. A browser-level change that preserved those strings would not be caught, and a direct configuration POST bypassing the page would not hit the page's explicit step check (OperationalLimits.Validate enforces only the byte range). This is the intended design per ADR-028 clause 1 (the step check is owned by the settings conversion/validation path, task 16.1), and it is disclosed in the test class XML documentation, the changelog, and the register as V12-G8-1. No overclaim is made.
findings.recommended_action: No change required for this task; the residual is correctly registered.
